name: Hymenolepis diminuta

taxonomy.rank_note: Reference groups can include multiple species. Protozoan higher-rank systems differ; the lineage is provided without forcing every clade into a class rank.

morphology: Egg: about 70–85 × 60–80 µm, yellowish, round to oval, with a six-hooked embryo and no polar filaments.
Adult intestinal tapeworms are primarily parasites of rodents.

transmission.detail: Arthropods ingest eggs; accidental ingestion of an arthropod containing a cysticercoid introduces infection.

life_cycle.detail: Arthropods ingest eggs; accidental ingestion of an arthropod containing a cysticercoid introduces infection.

hosts: Definitive: rodents, occasionally humans. Intermediate: grain beetles and other arthropods.
distribution: Worldwide sporadic human infection; consider accidental insect ingestion.
clinical_significance: Usually mild intestinal infection, occasionally abdominal pain or diarrhea.
diagnostics: Wet mount/concentration at 100–400×; document size and absence of filaments in well-focused eggs.
differential_diagnosis: Compare with smaller H. nana eggs bearing polar filaments and with nonparasitic pollen.
review_status: Source-compiled educational content; not independently clinically validated

annotation_guidance: Record specimen, stage, stain, objective/total magnification, pixel calibration, source image and reviewer certainty.
Native crops of 200–650 pixels do not determine biological size. Retain µm-per-pixel calibration before resizing.
Split training, validation and test data by patient/specimen; keep related crops in the same split.
Keep damaged or ambiguous objects uncertain. Molecular confirmation of a mixed specimen does not assign every pictured object a species.
